requirements.requirement: Node1 has an enabled, persistent host firewall.
requirements.summary: Firewalld was enabled and active before restart, the restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and firewalld recovered active with the same permanent and runtime rules.

requirements.requirement: SSH to node1 is allowed from any address.
requirements.summary: The active and permanent public zone contains the unrestricted SSH service, sshd listens on IPv4 and IPv6, and node2 and node3 both received SSH banners after the restart sequence.

requirements.requirement: TCP port 9000 on node1 is accepted only from node2 and rejected from node3 and all other sources, persistently.
requirements.summary: Permanent, runtime, and kernel rules place node2's IPv4 /32 acceptance before a source-independent TCP/9000 rejection. With a live listener, node2 received HTTP 200 while node3 was immediately rejected, including after node1 restarted and again after all managed-node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible firewall software.
requirements.summary: Node1 remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. The existing RHEL firewalld/nftables stack was used successfully, with no observed package-health damage.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Node1's persistent firewall preserves unrestricted SSH, accepts TCP/9000 only from node2, and rejects the catch-all remainder. The policy survived restart, the platform was retained, cleanup was complete, and every managed node passed the restart evidence protocol.
limitations: Behavioral source tests covered the two managed peers rather than arbitrary additional or IPv6 clients. The broader SSH and TCP/9000 scope is established by the observed unrestricted SSH service/listener bindings and source-independent catch-all reject rule.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The permanent rule additions and reload directly implemented the task. Transient HTTP listeners used for bounded behavioral tests were stopped and left no listener, unit-file, or temporary-file residue. The three restarts served persistence validation and the mandatory provider-wide restart protocol. All nodes finished without failed services and with healthy package state. Restart evidence is complete: each node has a healthy pre-state, scheduling acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered services, data checksums, networking, and relevant connectivity; fixed lifecycle boot identities corroborate all three transitions.
